key_insight: Treating transformer layers as a reusable library of functions, rather than a fixed-depth sequence, can improve LLM inference when inputs are dynamically routed through skips and repeats.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive layer routing can reduce wasted computation on easy inputs and allocate more depth to hard inputs, suggesting a path toward more efficient and controllable LLM inference.
method: Reconstructed and extended PoLar’s diagnostic MCTS-based routing algorithm.
Evaluated adaptive skip/repeat layer programs across 5 models.
Compared standard forward pass, skipping, repeating, combined routing, and learned-router top-k programs.
evidence_signal: Across five models, skipping beat the standard pass, repeating beat skipping, and skip+repeat was best; easier questions used shorter programs while harder ones needed more repeats.
watch_item: The learned single-shot router did not reliably improve top-1 inference, and many error-correcting programs were brittle to small edits, so deployment needs robustness checks.
paper_title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
